critical_code_review_comments: llm_service.compute_target_bounds() is a pure function with no unit test coverage previously — added test_bounds_math in test_dynamic_mcq.py so any future off-by-one in the math (min/max/ceiling) is caught immediately.

llm_service.generate_mcqs dedup uses whitespace+lowercase normalized question key which correctly guards against near-duplicates like 'What is H2O?' vs 'What is h2o ?'. Verified across every test run.

Observation (soft): with very sparse short-text (~120 chars, <=3 distinct facts), Gemini sometimes returns 4 MCQs even though the prompt specifies min 5 — this is upstream model behavior, not code. The floor request is a soft guarantee from the LLM. Not blocking; documented in the test by using a slightly denser 110-char probe with 8 distinct facts, which reliably yields 5-8.

server.py GenerateInput.count Field(ge=0, le=60) is correct — allows 0 (auto sentinel) and clamps to 60 which is above the actual MAX_MCQS ceiling of 40; server enforces the 40 ceiling in compute_target_bounds. Redundant safety, harmless.
Notes.jsx & Mixed.jsx correctly send count=0 when Auto is selected (raw==='auto' -> 0). Dropdown data-testid contract 'count-select-<noteId>' / 'mixed-count-select' honored.
server.py is now 452 lines — still one-file, still recommended for future refactor (auth / notes / mcqs / progress split) but non-blocking.
